newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia sends balanced budget draft to parliament.
newsitem.headline: Estonia sends balanced budget draft to parliament.

text.p: The Estonian government on Tuesday confirmed a balanced draft budget for 1997 and referred it to parliament for approval, Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi said.
The budget foresees spending of 15.1 billion kroons, a rise of 11 percent on last year.
A balanced budget is enforced by legislation in Estonia.
One of the biggest rises in spending is to be in defence, Vaehi told a news conference.
"We have promised to double defence spending and so in 1997 it will rise 42 percent compared with 1996," Vaehi said.
Spending on defence next year would be 700 million kroons, he added. The government also authorised the ministry of defence to borrow $20 million to buy military equipment.
The other main areas of spending are for the ministry of social affairs at 2.2 billion kroons, education 2.1 billion kroons and interior ministry 1.5 billion kroons.
The biggest revenue items are the sales tax, expected to raise 5.5 billion kroons, income tax 5.1 billion kroons and excise duties 2.3 billion kroons.
